questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following biphenyl derivatives is expected to have the HIGHEST barrier to racemization around the central $\text{C1}-\text{C1}'$ single bond?
questions.explanationEn: Atropisomerism in ortho-substituted biphenyls arises from steric hindrance to coplanarity in the transition state for rotation about the $\text{C1}-\text{C1}'$ bond. Among the ortho substituents compared, iodine ($-\text{I}$, van der Waals radius $\approx 1.98\text{ \AA}$) is vastly larger than $-\text{F}$ ($1.47\text{ \AA}$), $-\text{OH}$ ($1.52\text{ \AA}$), or $-\text{OMe}$. Paired with two bulky $-\text{NO}_2$ groups, 2,2'-diiodo-6,6'-dinitrobiphenyl has the largest steric barrier to rotation and highest racemization barrier.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In 1,2-difluoroethane ($\text{FCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{F}$), the gauche conformer is more stable than the anti conformer in the gas phase primarily due to:
optionsEn: Intramolecular hydrogen bonding between the two fluorine atoms
Hyperconjugative donation from filled $\sigma_{\text{C}-\text{H}}$ orbitals into low-lying antibonding $\sigma^*_{\text{C}-\text{F}}$ orbitals
Dipole-dipole attraction between the two parallel $\text{C}-\text{F}$ bonds
Reduced steric repulsion between the two fluorine atoms in the gauche conformation
questions.explanationEn: The gauche effect in 1,2-difluoroethane arises from stereoelectronic hyperconjugation: in the gauche conformation, each electron-rich $\sigma_{\text{C}-\text{H}}$ bonding orbital is aligned antiperiplanar ($180^\circ$) to a low-lying, strongly accepting $\sigma^*_{\text{C}-\text{F}}$ antibonding orbital, providing stabilizing $\sigma_{\text{C}-\text{H}} \to \sigma^*_{\text{C}-\text{F}}$ delocalization that outweighs steric and dipolar repulsions.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Among the following conjugated cyclic species, which one is classified as **antiaromatic** according to Hückel's rule (assuming planar geometry)?
questions.explanationEn: Planar, cyclic, completely conjugated systems with $(4n+2)\,\pi$ electrons are aromatic, whereas those with $4n\,\pi$ electrons are antiaromatic. Cyclopropenyl cation ($2\,\pi$), cyclopentadienyl anion ($6\,\pi$), and tropylium cation ($6\,\pi$) all obey $(4n+2)$ and are aromatic. The cyclopentadienyl cation ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_5^+$) has $4\,\pi$ electrons ($n = 1$) in a planar conjugated ring and is therefore antiaromatic.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In an elimination reaction, replacing the $\beta$-hydrogen with deuterium lowers the reaction rate by a factor of $k_H / k_D = 6.5$ at $298\text{ K}$. This observation provides strong evidence that:
optionsEn: The reaction follows an $E1$ mechanism with rate-determining carbocation formation
The $\text{C}-\text{H}$ bond is broken in the rate-determining step (consistent with a concerted $E2$ mechanism)
The reaction proceeds via a rapid, reversible pre-equilibrium deprotonation ($E1\text{cb}_{\text{rev}}$)
Only a secondary kinetic isotope effect is operating
questions.explanationEn: A large primary kinetic isotope effect ($k_H/k_D \approx 6\text{--}7$ at $298\text{ K}$) arises from the difference in zero-point vibrational energies between $\text{C}-\text{H}$ and $\text{C}-\text{D}$ stretching modes and is observed only when the $\text{C}-\text{H}$ bond is significantly cleaved in the rate-determining transition state, as in a concerted $E2$ elimination (or irreversible $E1\text{cb}$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following bridgehead carbocations is the LEAST stable (slowest to form in $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ solvolysis of its corresponding bromide)?
questions.explanationEn: Carbocations strongly prefer trigonal planar ($sp^2$) geometry. In rigid bicyclic cages, flattening the bridgehead carbon introduces severe angle strain. The smaller, more rigid bicyclo[2.2.1]hept-1-yl (1-norbornyl) skeleton resists flattening far more strongly than bicyclo[2.2.2]oct-1-yl or 1-adamantyl, making 1-norbornyl cation the least stable (solvolysis of 1-bromonorbornane is $\sim 10^{14}$ times slower than *tert*-butyl bromide).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements regarding the conformational analysis of substituted cyclohexanes are CORRECT?
optionsEn: The $A$-value of an ethynyl group ($-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$) is smaller than that of a methyl group ($-\text{CH}_3$)
In *cis*-1-methyl-4-*tert*-butylcyclohexane, the methyl group is locked in the axial position
The $A$-value of $-\text{I}$ is significantly larger than that of $-\text{CH}_3$
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: The linear $-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$ group ($A \approx 0.41\text{ kcal mol}^{-1}$) projects straight out with minimal 1,3-diaxial steric clash compared to $-\text{CH}_3$ ($A \approx 1.74\text{ kcal mol}^{-1}$). (B) True: Because $^t\text{Bu}$ ($A \approx 4.9\text{ kcal mol}^{-1}$) locks the ring equatorially, the *cis*-1,4-methyl must sit axially. (C) True: *trans*-1,4-Dimethylcyclohexane is diequatorial ($0$ axial methyls), whereas the *cis* isomer has one axial methyl. (D) False: Despite iodine's large radius, its very long $\text{C}-\text{I}$ bond ($2.14\text{ \AA}$) places it far from the 1,3-diaxial hydrogens, giving $A(-\text{I}) \approx 0.43\text{ kcal mol}^{-1} \ll A(-\text{CH}_3)$. Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following substrates exhibit strong neighboring group participation (anchimeric assistance) during solvolysis?
questions.explanationEn: (A) Correct: Sulfur in $\text{EtSCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ is a soft, polarizable nucleophile that rapidly displaces $\text{Cl}^-$ intramolecularly to form a cyclic episulfonium ion, accelerating solvolysis by $\sim 10^4$-fold. (B) Correct: In *trans*-2-acetoxycyclohexyl tosylate, the acetoxy group can adopt an antiperiplanar (diaxial) geometry to the leaving $-\text{OTs}$ group, forming a cyclic acetoxonium ion with retention of configuration. (C) Incorrect: In the *cis* isomer, $-\text{OAc}$ and $-\text{OTs}$ cannot achieve a *trans*-diaxial arrangement. (D) Incorrect: Oxygen in $\text{EtOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ is less nucleophilic and inductively slows solvolysis rather than providing strong NGP. Hence, (A) and (B) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of stereoisomers possible for 2,3,4-trihydroxypentanedioic acid ($\text{HO}_2\text{C}-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$) is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: This symmetric molecule has two equivalent terminal stereocenters (C2, C4) and a central carbon (C3). There are $2$ optically active enantiomers: $(2R,4R)$ and $(2S,4S)$ (where C3 is not stereogenic), plus $2$ distinct achiral *meso* diastereomers: $(2R,3r,4S)$ and $(2R,3s,4S)$ (where C3 is a pseudoasymmetric center). Total stereoisomers $= 2 + 2 = 4$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: According to Hückel molecular orbital theory (Frost circle), the total number of $\pi$-bonding molecular orbitals (with energy $E < \alpha$) in the tropylium cation ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_7^+$) is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Inscribing a regular heptagon with one vertex pointing straight down in a Frost circle of radius $2|\beta|$ places $1$ lowest-energy non-degenerate MO at $\alpha + 2\beta$ and $1$ doubly degenerate pair of bonding MOs at $\alpha + 2\beta\cos(2\pi/7) = \alpha + 1.247\beta$ (all below the non-bonding line $E = \alpha$), while the remaining $4$ MOs lie above $\alpha$ (antibonding). Thus, there are $1 + 2 = 3$ bonding $\pi$-MOs.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of $\alpha$-$\text{C}-\text{H}$ bonds available for hyperconjugation in the 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-yl carbocation ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}^+-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$) is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Hyperconjugation in a carbocation involves donation from adjacent $\alpha$-$\text{C}-\text{H}$ $\sigma$-bonds into the vacant $2p$ orbital of the positively charged carbon. The 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-yl cation has two directly attached $-\text{CH}_3$ groups ($2 \times 3 = 6$ $\alpha$-$\text{C}-\text{H}$ bonds) and one attached isopropyl group $-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ ($1$ $\alpha$-$\text{C}-\text{H}$ bond at C3), giving a total of $6 + 1 = 7$ hyperconjugable $\alpha$-$\text{C}-\text{H}$ bonds.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Consider the two pairs of protons in citric acid, $\text{HO}_2\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(\text{OH})(\text{CO}_2\text{H})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$: let $\text{H}_a$ and $\text{H}_b$ be the two geminal protons on the same $-\text{CH}_2-$ group (C2), and let $\text{C2}$ and $\text{C4}$ be the two $-\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ arms. The correct relationships are:
optionsEn: $\text{H}_a$ and $\text{H}_b$ are enantiotopic; the two $-\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ arms are homotopic
$\text{H}_a$ and $\text{H}_b$ are diastereotopic; the two $-\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ arms are enantiotopic
$\text{H}_a$ and $\text{H}_b$ are homotopic; the two $-\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ arms are enantiotopic
$\text{H}_a$ and $\text{H}_b$ are diastereotopic; the two $-\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ arms are diastereotopic
questions.explanationEn: Citric acid has $C_s$ symmetry with a mirror plane passing through C3, $-\text{OH}$, and the central $-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, which reflects the C2 arm into the C4 arm (and lacks any $C_2$ axis); therefore, the two $-\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ arms are **enantiotopic** (making C3 prochiral). On a single methylene carbon (C2), replacing $\text{H}_a$ vs $\text{H}_b$ with deuterium creates a stereocenter at C2 AND simultaneously renders C3 stereogenic, producing a pair of diastereomers; hence $\text{H}_a$ and $\text{H}_b$ are **diastereotopic**.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: When *trans*-2-decalone is treated with $\text{Br}_2$ in glacial acetic acid (acid-catalyzed enolization), the major monobrominated product is:
questions.explanationEn: In *trans*-2-decalone, acid-catalyzed bromination proceeds via the thermodynamically more stable enol. Introducing a $\Delta^{2,3}$ double bond (between C2 and C3) relieves eclipsing interactions and forms a less strained *trans*-octalin-like ring, whereas a $\Delta^{1,2}$ double bond introduces unfavorable steric/torsional strain with the C9/C10 ring junction (classic Corey/Velluz selectivity in 3-keto-$5\alpha$-steroids and *trans*-2-decalones). Hence, enolization occurs predominantly toward C3, giving 3-bromo-*trans*-2-decalone.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the electrophilic aromatic nitration of benzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$) vs hexadeuteriobenzene ($\text{C}_6\text{D}_6$) with $\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, the observed kinetic isotope effect is $k_H / k_D \approx 1.0$, whereas in the sulfonation of benzene with fuming $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, $k_H / k_D \approx 1.7$. The best mechanistic explanation is:
optionsEn: In nitration, $\text{C}-\text{H}$ bond cleavage is fast and occurs after the rate-determining formation of the Wheland $\sigma$-complex; in sulfonation, $\text{C}-\text{H}$ deprotonation is partially rate-determining due to reversible $\sigma$-complex formation
Nitration proceeds by a radical mechanism while sulfonation proceeds by an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism
Both reactions have rate-determining $\text{C}-\text{H}$ cleavage, but $\text{SO}_3$ is heavier than $\text{NO}_2^+$
In nitration, formation of $\text{NO}_2^+$ is irreversible and $\text{C}-\text{H}$ is never broken
questions.explanationEn: In electrophilic aromatic nitration, addition of $\text{NO}_2^+$ to form the Wheland arenium $\sigma$-complex is the slow, rate-determining step ($k_2 \gg k_{-1}$), so subsequent deprotonation does not affect the rate ($k_H/k_D \approx 1.0$). In sulfonation, formation of the $\sigma$-complex is reversible ($k_{-1}$ is comparable to $k_2$), making the proton-loss step partially rate-determining and yielding a small primary KIE ($k_H/k_D \approx 1.7$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following anions is the MOST stable (corresponds to the most acidic conjugate acid)?
questions.explanationEn: Comparing the $\text{p}K_a$ values (in DMSO) of the conjugate acids: cyclopentadiene ($\text{p}K_a \approx 18.0$) $<$ indene ($\text{p}K_a \approx 20.1$) $<$ fluorene ($\text{p}K_a \approx 22.6$) $\ll$ cycloheptatriene ($\text{p}K_a \approx 36$, antiaromatic $8\pi$ anion). Cyclopentadienyl anion gains the full $6\pi$-aromatic stabilization energy of a pristine cyclopentadienyl ring, whereas benzo-annulation in indenyl and fluorenyl anions lowers the net aromatic stabilization gain because delocalization perturbs the existing benzene sextets. Hence, cyclopentadienyl anion is the most stable.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following annulenes is **non-aromatic** at room temperature due to severe transannular $\text{H}\cdots\text{H}$ steric repulsion forcing it out of planarity, despite possessing $(4n+2)\,\pi$ electrons?
questions.explanationEn: Although [10]annulene has $10\,\pi$ electrons ($4n+2$ with $n = 2$), the all-*cis* isomer suffers severe angle strain ($144^\circ$ vs $120^\circ$) and the *cis,trans,cis,cis,trans* isomer suffers severe transannular steric clash between the two internal hydrogens, forcing the ring out of planarity and rendering [10]annulene **non-aromatic**. By contrast, bridging the two internal carbons with a $-\text{CH}_2-$ group (1,6-methano[10]annulene) removes the internal hydrogens and restores aromaticity, and both [14]annulene and [18]annulene are large enough to be nearly planar and aromatic.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements regarding the anomeric effect in carbohydrate and heterocyclic chemistry are CORRECT?
optionsEn: In D-glucopyranose in water, the $\beta$-anomer ($\sim 64\%$) predominates over the $\alpha$-anomer ($\sim 36\%$), whereas in D-mannopyranose in water, the $\alpha$-anomer ($\sim 67\%$) predominates over the $\beta$-anomer ($\sim 33\%$)
The $\text{C1}-\text{O5}$ ring bond is shorter and the $\text{C1}-\text{X}$ exocyclic bond is longer in the axial anomer than in the equatorial anomer of 2-chlorotetrahydropyran
The magnitude of the endo-anomeric effect increases as the dielectric constant (polarity) of the solvent increases
In D-mannopyranose, the axial C2$-\text{OH}$ introduces a destabilizing $\Delta 2$ dipolar/steric effect in the $\beta$-anomer, further favoring the $\alpha$-anomer
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: In water, $\beta$-D-glucopyranose ($64\%$) is favored over $\alpha$ ($36\%$) because hydration reduces the anomeric effect relative to the steric preference of $-\text{OH}$, whereas in D-mannopyranose the axial C2$-\text{OH}$ creates an unfavorable $\Delta 2$ effect in the $\beta$-anomer, making $\alpha$-D-mannopyranose ($67\%$) predominate (D is also true). (B) True: $n_{\text{O5}} \to \sigma^*_{\text{C1}-\text{X}}$ hyperconjugation increases the $\text{C1}-\text{O5}$ double-bond character (shortening it) and weakens/lengthens the $\text{C1}-\text{X}$ bond. (C) False: Polar solvents stabilize the higher-dipole equatorial conformer more strongly, *decreasing* the magnitude of the anomeric effect. Hence, (A), (B), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following reactions proceed via a **benzyne** (aryne) intermediate?
optionsEn: Treatment of chlorobenzene with $\text{NaNH}_2$ in liquid $\text{NH}_3$ at $-33\,^\circ\text{C}$
Heating anthranilic acid (2-aminobenzoic acid) with isoamyl nitrite ($^i\text{AmONO}$) in the presence of furan
questions.explanationEn: (A) Correct: Strong amide base induces 1,2-elimination of $\text{HCl}$ from chlorobenzene to generate benzyne. (B) Correct: Diazotization of anthranilic acid yields benzenediazonium-2-carboxylate, which extrudes $\text{N}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ thermally to form benzyne (trapped by furan via Diels-Alder). (C) Incorrect: 2,4-Dinitrochlorobenzene reacts via the addition-elimination $\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$ mechanism through a Meisenheimer complex, not benzyne. (D) Correct: Fluoride-induced elimination of $\text{Me}_3\text{SiF}$ and $\text{TfO}^-$ (Kobayashi method) cleanly generates benzyne. Hence, (A), (B), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ solvolysis of *para*-substituted 1-phenylethyl chlorides at $298\text{ K}$, the first-order rate constants for the *para*-methoxy ($\sigma_p = -0.27$) and *para*-cyano ($\sigma_p = +0.66$) derivatives are $8.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ s}^{-1}$ and $8.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ s}^{-1}$, respectively. The Hammett reaction constant $\rho$ for this reaction is _____ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanationEn: From the Hammett equation $\log_{10}(k_X / k_H) = \rho \sigma_X$, taking the difference between the two derivatives yields $\log_{10}(k_{p\text{-CN}} / k_{p\text{-OMe}}) = \rho(\sigma_{p\text{-CN}} - \sigma_{p\text{-OMe}})$. Substituting the values: $\log_{10}(8.0 \times 10^{-6} / 8.0 \times 10^{-3}) = \log_{10}(10^{-3}) = -3.00$, and $\Delta\sigma = 0.66 - (-0.27) = 0.93$. Therefore, $\rho = \frac{-3.00}{0.93} = -3.23$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The base-catalyzed hydrolysis of ethyl aliphatic esters ($\text{RCO}_2\text{Et}$) obeys the Taft equation $\log_{10}(k_R / k_{\text{Me}}) = \rho^* \sigma^* + \delta E_s$ with $\rho^* = +2.50$ and $\delta = +1.00$. Given that for $\text{R} = -\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$, $\sigma^* = +1.05$ and $E_s = -0.24$, the ratio of hydrolysis rate constants $k_{\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}} / k_{\text{CH}_3}$ is _____ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanationEn: Substituting the parameters into the Taft equation: $\log_{10}(k_{\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}} / k_{\text{CH}_3}) = (+2.50)(+1.05) + (+1.00)(-0.24) = 2.625 - 0.240 = 2.385$. Taking the antilogarithm yields $k_{\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}} / k_{\text{CH}_3} = 10^{2.385} = 242.66 \approx 243$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Stereochemistry, Conformations & Reaction Mechanisms (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A solution of an optically pure atropisomeric biphenyl exhibits an initial optical rotation of $+12.0^\circ$ at $320\text{ K}$. After $40.0\text{ min}$ at $320\text{ K}$, the optical rotation decreases to $+3.0^\circ$ due to thermal racemization ($\text{R}_a \underset{k_{\text{inv}}}{\overset{k_{\text{inv}}}{\rightleftharpoons}} \text{S}_a$). The first-order rate constant for single-enantiomer inversion, $k_{\text{inv}}$ (in $\text{min}^{-1}$), is _____ (rounded off to four decimal places).
questions.explanationEn: The decay of optical rotation follows $\alpha(t) = \alpha(0) e^{-k_{\text{rac}} t}$, where the racemization rate constant is $k_{\text{rac}} = 2 k_{\text{inv}}$ because each inversion event converts one $(+)$-molecule into a $(-)$-molecule, reducing the enantiomeric excess by $2$. Thus, $\frac{3.0}{12.0} = \frac{1}{4} = e^{-k_{\text{rac}} \times 40.0} \implies k_{\text{rac}} = \frac{\ln 4}{40.0} = 0.03466\text{ min}^{-1}$. Dividing by $2$ gives $k_{\text{inv}} = \frac{k_{\text{rac}}}{2} = \frac{\ln 2}{40.0} = 0.0173\text{ min}^{-1}$.
